text.p: LME copper breached resistance on Tuesday, shrugging off a substantial inventory rise as the market was hit by renewed physical tightness in Europe.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index was 0.28 points higher at 242.37.

Three month copper prices paused following the release of stocks data that showed a 11,475 tonne rise, but went on to steadily push up through resistance levels of $2,200 and $2,215. The market ended the afternoon kerb at $2,221, up $26 and just $3 off its high. The premium of cash over three months metal firmed by about $15 to $120/$130. Resistance was pegged at $2,240/50, then the November 28 high of $2,313.

Nickel put in another good showing on Tuesday, galloping up by $220 to finish the kerb at $7,080, right in the middle of a resistance area based on previous highs of $7,090 and $7,070 on November 26 and 27 respectively. The market lifted off on Monday on technical buying and short-covering after becoming oversold, erasing a whole month of losses in two days. Prices would now have to grind down a band of resistance between $7,170 and $7,250 to make further progress, Bahr said.

Aluminium finished the day $8.50 firmer at $1,560.50, ending near it highs but failing to confront important resistance at $1,570. The market was rangebound and needed more time to consolidate before breaking higher, analysts say.
Tin closed the kerb $40 stronger at $5,800 and zinc ended $8 firmer at $1,072
Lead finishing barely changed at $695, down $1, while aluminium alloy finished stronger at $1,445 versus $1,430/35.

New York precious metals futures were steady at higher levels midday, after some shortcovering helped the precious metals complex to stabilize after four days of heavy falls, traders said. "A bounce is not a surprise from such an oversold condition, and it makes sense for the funds to cover some shorts now the $360 level has been achieved, but the floor has gone quiet again now which is a bit of a worry," North American Equity Services floor trader John Geraghty said. COMEX February gold was up $1.30 an ounce at $360.00 midday, after seeing a $358.40-360.70 morning range. Spot gold in the bullion market was quoted $358.60/359.10 midday, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $35

CBOT wheat futures were slightly higher at midsession Tuesday on ideas that sub-zero temperatures forecast for the U.S. this weekend could damage the wheat crop, traders said. Temperatures in Kansas are forecast to fall below zero this weekend. Because the hard red winter wheat crop has little or no snow cover, it could be vulnerable to winterkill damage, floor traders said. At 1158 CST, CBOT wheat futures were 1/2 to two cents per bushel higher, with March up 1/2 at $3.89 and May up 1-1/4 at $3.68-1/2.

CSCE world sugar prices slumped in early going Tuesday, led by sharp losses on the spot contract, as dealers sold heavily in response to Commitment of Traders data released last night, trading sources said. The latest CFTC figures, which showed speculators to be net long nearly 24,000 lots (non-commercial plus non-reportable) as of December 31, sparked a rapid sell-off this morning. At 1137 EST, March futures were down 0.19 cent a lb, to 10.88 cents, having traded from 10.84 to 10.99. May was 0.13 lower, at 10.97, while the outer months were 0.04 to 0.12 lower.

NYMEX heating oil fell on profit-taking Tuesday morning, pushing crude and gasoline into lower rangebound trade, traders said. "A lot of people got in yesterday between 73.25 and 72.25, and so they got out early before we started to hover around 73.10," said a New York heating oil dealer. At 1130 EST, February heating oil was off 0.74 cent a gallon at 72.90 cents. Feb crude was off 17 cents at $26.20 a barrel.
